utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. While the witness is being brought in, could I mention that in the oral decision given yesterday, I referred to the wrong two pages of the transcript. It should have been pages 3 and 4 to which access is granted. And could I add that to speed things up and smooth the process, the Chamber has made available the relevant documents to the Defence already. So there's no need for any further compliance with the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. And now for a change, it's Mr. Djurdjic who has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team of the accused Vlastimir Djordjevic and here with me I have madam Marie O'Leary and Mr. Popovic. Mr. Cvetic, both of us will have a problem today because both of us tend to speak rather quickly and to make things more difficult we both use the same language. In order for us and the courtroom to be able to understand everything and in order for the transcript to be correct, I would kindly ask you and I will do this myself, please try to speak slowly and try to wait for me to finish so that we do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to correct some things from yesterday's transcript where I believe that some things were entered wrongly. First of all, could you please tell me, between mid-1998 and until the moment when you left SUP Kosovska Mitrovica, what was the position of Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was assistant minister, that is, head of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Another thing, at the staff meeting which was held, I believe you said, on March the 8th, was there the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslavia army?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And yet another thing, but I can't really translate the question of Mr. Stamp, but I want to ask the following: Could you know on the 1st of July what kind of telegram were you going to receive from the staff on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All this is on page 6715 of the transcript and it regards the Exhibit P1054 and P1052.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvetic, for your answers.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, would I like to start from some legislation, some general acts that were in force in Ministry of the Interior in the Republic of Serbia during the relevant period. Just to make sure, whenever I ask anything, it refers to the period between mid-1998 and the end of the war, and I will specify all the other time-periods.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you are saying mid-1998, are you talking June 1998 until the end of the period which I was present in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I will refer to any other time-periods. I will specify that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the Exhibit P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is the Law on Internal Affairs. Page 1 in B/C/S version and page 2 in the English version, Article 6, Mr. Cvetic. Am I right to say that on the basis of this article, it was the minister who decided on the formation of organisational units both in the seat and he decided on the territories for which organisational units were formed.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but could I please check that we are talking about the law that was in effect at the time, but when you said that -- what you said is absolutely correct, but could we just check that this is the relevant act that was in effect that year because there were quite a lot of amendments. So could I please see what is the number of the Official Gazette because I know what the number of the Official Gazette should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the Court Officer scroll this up in order to check. No, please, down, just a bit down. No, no, could you please take it down so scroll down just a bit. Scroll down. Yes. And now if you could go to the left. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you can see that this is the Official Gazette of the Republic of Serbia, 54/96?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can we proceed, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment on Article 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could have Article 7 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The minister shall determine the manner in which the Ministry of the Interior performs its duties and issue instructions for their performance." And yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right, Mr. Cvetic to say that upon the request of the People's Assembly and the request of the president of the republic, the minister reported on the work of the ministry and the security situation in the republic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are absolutely right. Not only upon the request of the president of the republic and the Assembly, but also upon the request of the government of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, this is clear enough because the president, he was a member of the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 5 in the English version and page 2 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, Article 18, 19, and 20, do they regulate the persons that were authorised officials, and also the rights of the uniformed members of the police?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm particularly interested in Article 20 if you could comment on it.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 20 stipulates as follows: "An authorised official must perform duties relating to the security of this republic, protection of the life and safety of citizens and their property, prevention and detection of criminal offences and apprehension of perpetrators, regardless whether or not he is on official duty and whether or not he has been given such a task." That is paragraph 1. And paragraph 2 says: "An authorised official must form the tasks referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article even when his personal safety is at risk." And this is all correct. This is stipulated not only by law but also by the regulation on public security service.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, a correction in the transcript, line 5 on page 51 [sic], there should be "minister" instead of "president."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, since we have these provisions, there is no read to read them out, you can read them for yourself and possibly just comment or make certain explanations.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I cannot comment on the text of the law. I can simply say whether it was applied or not. I'm not authorised to comment on any legislation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, this is exactly what I meant, whether you know if this was applied in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see Article 28 in B/C/S; this is page 3. And in the English version it's on page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, these are the provision on the reserve forces, so Articles 28 and 29, and I believe there is some misunderstanding here, so I would like to clarify this. Could you please explain what reserve forces really are in line with Articles 28 and 29 of this law?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that in line with the act on systematisation of jobs at the Ministry of the Interior, we had a certain number of police forces and this applied to peacetimes. However, given that at the level of the republic the estimates of danger of risks were made, sometimes in certain parts of the republic, or in the entire republic; the public security and order could be at risk. There could be a risk of inter-ethical conflicts or the risk of terrorist attacks. For that reason, still at peacetime, the peacetime forces would be inefficient and this is why estimates were made on the necessities concerning reserve forces. So we had peacetime formation and we also had a schematic of the organisation and systematisation for peacetime; but we also had the schematic of organisation and systemisation for the period of imminent threat of war, state of war, and other extraordinary situations. So the peacetime formation of the police would be replenished with certain number of people that belonged to the reserve forces. This replenishment was done through competent military territorial organisations in the following way: The Secretariats were submitting their requests to the competent military territorial body, and they stipulated the number of persons and of which particular specialties they needed in order to replenish their units. Once they replenished their units with members of the reserve forces, the decision on the engagement of these reserve forces was made by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The members of the reserve forces, until the moment when they were engaged by the minister, were civilians carrying out their regular civilian duties?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When engaged, these persons had had the same status as regular police officers who were employed by MUP, so they were authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had the same authorities as active members of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were they entitled to other things, such as health care?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we seem to be proceeding too quickly. So were they entitled to social -- to social entitlements, were they entitled to health care, reimbursement of per diems and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had the same entitlements as members of the active forces. They even could have increased credit for the years of service and so some time in the future they could use this when their retirement was to be calculated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So I'll have to ask for that increased credit for my years of service?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, while you are contemplating that joyful prospect, could I correct a transcript which records your correction incorrectly. You mentioned much earlier that there was a "president" recorded instead of "minister," in the transcript. That should have been at page 5, line 1. Not as you are recorded as saying line 5, page 21 -- 51. With a bit of luck between us, we will now have the minister in the right place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to add, the issue of these reserve forces, if we want to complete the legislative stipulation concerning this, there is yet another instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness, we will come to that later on because of our procedure. But can we now explain, members of the police reserve squads, am I right to say that these persons did not have the status of authorised officials pursuant to the Law on the Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that these people do not have the same rights to salary, per diem, health insurance, and other insurance?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that those are people who pursue their regular jobs, and in their place of residence carry out the defence of their population centres?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these people are not members of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or rather, to be quite precise, they are not employed with the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just one last question on this: When immobilisation call-up is announced, do these people have to report to the units where they have a wartime assignment?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please show page 11 in B/C/S. Sorry, page 4 in B/C/S and page 11 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me something about this Article 33?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This provision of Article 33 of the Law on Internal Affairs states that the employees of the Ministry of the Interior are obliged to carry out all the orders of the minister except for those orders which constitute a criminal offence. This applies not only to the Ministry of the Interior. This applies to all the ministries in the Republic of Serbia and all this is governed by the law on the work of state authorities. That means that employees in all the ministries are duty-bound to carry out all the orders of their superiors apart from those which constitute crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have page 5 in B/C/S and page 16 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'd like to know, Mr. Cvetic, about Articles 51, 52, and 53. These are the basic provisions governing disciplinary liability and disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: They were later specified by the decree on disciplinary proceedings and the wartime decree on the same?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we need page 17 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me first explain paragraph 1 of Article 56. An employee shall be removed from the Ministry of the Interior if criminal proceedings have been instituted against him for criminal charges stipulated in Article 34, paragraph 1, item 1 of this law. So there is no other possibility. The person shall be removed. And the second paragraph says, An employee may be removed from the ministry when criminal proceedings have been instituted against him for criminal charges that are subject to prosecution ex officio, or when disciplinary proceedings have been instituted against him for serious violation of work obligations and duties. So it is up to the superior in this case to decide whether to remove the offender or not. Whereas in the first paragraph, it says explicitly that the person has to be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, let me go back a little. When it is established that an employee of the Ministry of the Interior is guilty of a serious crime, am I right that this has nothing to do with remand in police custody that is decided in pre-indictment proceedings at the SUP or with the remand in custody in pre-trial proceedings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, Article 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is page 6 in B/C/S and 21 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm very familiar with this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This stipulates the basis for sending an employee of the MUP to other organisational units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But here in this provision, the reason, the basis for sending -- for seconding an employee of the MUP elsewhere has to be explicitly explained, otherwise in some cases it is up to the minister or chief of section whether to do this with certain employees -- not do this. What I am trying to say? A person who is sent to perform security jobs in Kosovo and Metohija, in the decision to send that person, it must be stated exactly for which period this is done, and the lawmaker says that this period may be at least 30 days but no more than one year. More than one year would be contrary to the law. There was some decisions when this is specified and other decisions where it is not specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But every individual decision to send a person elsewhere could be appealed to the minister of the interior; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's a different procedure. What -- how this complaint is handled, we need to explain this until the end. Usually when a decision is appealed, the appeal is unsuccessful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, every decision can be appealed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but every decision could be appealed to the minister within eight days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P357.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is the real -- clean version of the rules of the internal -- on the internal organisation of the Ministry of Interior that was in effect at the time. Do you agree it's the right one?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, although there were amendments later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, including in end 1999. You have already explained Article 2. Article 3 is local jurisdiction of Secretariats; we won't go through that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to Article 5, that's page 6. In fact, 8 in B/C/S; 8 in English it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Anyway, I'm interested in Article 5. Could you comment on Article 5. I would like you to explain this bit, OUPs, Departments of Internal Affairs and Secretariats do their work immediately in the territory where they are based?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A Secretariat of Internal Affairs is established as an internal organisational unit to the Ministry of the Interior to handle Internal Affairs for a certain number of municipalities. Territorially speaking, these were usually districts. Let's take a specific example. The SUP Kosovska Mitrovica was organised to handle Internal Affairs in the district of Kosovska Mitrovica. That was true of all the other districts and SUPs. Each Secretariat had smaller organisational units that were called departments of Internal Affairs, and police stations in municipalities. What would this depend on? On the size of the territory and the complexity of the security situation. If a municipality is smaller and suffers from no major security problems, such municipalities would have police stations. But police stations were organisationally linked, belonged to the Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could we now look at Article 6.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it's all correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the minister of the interior was authorised to make decisions to set up specialised and Special Police units, operations groups, and other specialised units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minister could do it himself, or he could authorise another person to do it; but the authorised person could not do it without the minister's consent.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So even if this is done but an authorised person, the minister is answerable?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Because the person was acting on the authority of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at Article 7. We have the right page in English, but in B/C/S I believe it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see well on this monitor, but I can suppose what it's about because I'm familiar with this subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we make it a bit larger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This article governs sectors and administrations in the ministry?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And their responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that since there are two sectors, public security and state security, the only person above both is the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that members of one sector may not issue assignments to members of the other sector?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these sectors are completely separate. These are completely separate services with different methods of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that only the minister by his own decision can create a body involving members of both sectors and identify their assignments and methods of work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: When you said that in 1998 an intersectorial body of the MUP was formed, and you were talking about that in relation to Adem Jashari, am I right in saying that this decision was made by the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The creation of an intersectorial body is the responsibility of the minister, and the minister appointed chief of the state security sector at the head of this body and his deputy was chief of the public security sector, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. And the chief of the state security sector was Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel now repeat the numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have page 9 in English and look at Article 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You should be an expert for this article.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I could not call myself an expert, but I was working with this for a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Explain this Article 9, please. Especially how it worked in practice; practice is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in a bit. I am sorry, I have not made a hard copy. And Mr. Stamp won't give me a hard copy, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's not long; you can answer. We are waiting for you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I was waiting for your okay. Every sector in the ministry, every organisational unit in the ministry, was preparing, even during peacetime, to act in the event of immediate threat of war, state of war, and other contingencies. Every sector, every organisational unit, and every administration prepared its plan of defence. This plan of defence contained the following: A security evaluation, plan of readiness, plan of mobilisation, plan of employment of forces and resources, plan of defence of population, plan of security measures, and plan of organisation of communications security, and plan of measures of alert. This was done so that when immediate threat of war is proclaimed, the units can immediately start putting into effect these plans, and, of course, special assignments are also involved in emergency situations. To proclaim the state of immediate threat of war and the state of war was the exclusive right of the National Assembly, but every segment of the defence system made these plans of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the seat of the ministry, was there a particular administration which had a particular unit dealing with this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the seat of the ministry, there was a section for defence planning.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about every SUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every SUP there was a person in charge of that desk. He was called inspector for defence planning, defence preparations. And this was part of the police department which is a smaller unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did these contingency plans arise from the defence plan?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at Article 10. This is all right in the English version, the page is all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me just repeat my last question: Were these contingency plans made pursuant to the federal Law on Defence?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look at Article 10.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please add, not only law but there was a range of bylaws as well, different instructions, orders, methodological instructions, so there were quite a lot of regulations that belonged to bylaws. They were different acts and different coordination that needed to be made between military territorial commands and different other bodies of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cvetic, could you now take a look at Article 10, please.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this is all correct, and this was applied in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this article which regulates the authority of the chief of the sector or chief of Secretariat, that they could set up permanent or ad hoc staffs, and it further on stipulates the conditions under which this could be done?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in practice, chief of Secretariats had no need to set up staffs, though the lawmaker provided for this possibility. The Secretariats usually set up commissions or Working Groups to analyse certain situations or decide on measures and actives.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please focus your attention on paragraph 2 now which talks about composition, tasks, dead-lines, powers, and other conditions contained in paragraph 1 of this article. So within the scope of their activity or the order received from the minister, these could be decided on by the chief of the sector. And it goes on and says so they have to include all this in a document and inform minister immediately?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Later on we will in practice come back to this article on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was not merely practice. This is the way in which it was stipulated by law. In other ministries they had similar practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now take a look at Article 12, please. It's on the same page in B/C/S version, and in the English version this is on the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, could you please tell us what this article actually meant in practice? What does it mean that Secretariats shall carry out all tasks in the sphere of the ministry as established in these rules and that they are responsible for the security situation in the area for which they have been established?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were responsible for the security situation, for public law and order situation pertaining to crime, traffic, also fire-fighting, aliens, and also the situation pertaining to the -- to people exercising their rights in front of various bodies of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I'm talking about only one segment of the security, so I'm only talking about public security here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, obviously these are the rules on the internal organisation of the public security sector, and earlier on I believe it was stipulated that the state security was to be stipulated in another set of rules. Am I right to say that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, could you please tell us what were the internal organisational units of the SUP Kosovska Mitrovica at the time when you were there? I'm not talking about OUPs and police stations, I'm talking about the seat of SUP.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The internal organisational units of the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica at its seat were at follows: The police department, the Crime Police Department, the department for aliens and passports, the fire-fighting police department, and department for general and joined affairs, and also we had a traffic police section. Within the police department, we also had a police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to save some time, let me ask you the following: Apart from carrying out duties pertaining to the Internal Affairs in accordance with the law and the rules, what was your relationship towards the local administration, local authorities district, and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a chief of the Secretariat, I was in contact with the head of the district and presidents of municipalities. And at these meetings and in our mutual conducts, we obviously analysed the security situation in the region. And presidents of municipality shared some security related problems with me, those that they had in their respective territories. But presidents of municipalities and head of the district were not authorised to issue any specific tasks to the chief of the Secretariat. However, they could ask from the chief of the Secretariat to engage certain units, to secure certain facilities or certain roads; but the procedure for doing that was very clearly stipulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems to me that in certain occasions when the conditions were met, when there were occurrences that were interesting for a specific territory, you were obliged to inform the chief of the specific district or president of the municipality about this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They received this on a daily basis, this information, the head of the district and presidents of the municipalities, they received it -- the head of district received it were SUP and presidents of municipalities received that from OUPs or police stations in their respective municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have the Exhibit P69.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is the law on state administration. Article 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English this is on page 2, and in B/C/S this is on page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I can't see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have both versions in English. Could we please have B/C/S version on one side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But let me read out Article 43 for you, it stipulates as follows: "The minister shall exercise the rights and duties specified in the constitution and the law and shall be in charge of the work of his ministry in conformity with this law."

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absolutely true, and this applied to all the ministries in the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that Article 44 specifies that the minister was to organise and ensure the lawful and effective performance of tasks and that he was to decide on the rights, duties, and responsibilities of employees?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And this is the basis for the adoption of the rules on disciplinary responsibility, disciplinary procedures, and some other rules which could be only adopted by the minister in MUP for example?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In Article 44, paragraph 2, it also specifies that the minister was responsible for carrying out the function that he has been entrusted and for the work of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that on my monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the following page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Since minister was a member of the government, he answered to the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you please take a look at Article 46. Am I right to say that this article stipulates, or rather, regulates the status of assistant ministers; and in the second paragraph, it stipulates who shall appoint the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was done by the government following the proposal of the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Another thing, the minister was to determine in which particular areas his assistants were to assist him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister decided which particular assistants were going to help him in which areas of his responsibilities, and he proposed these ministers to the government, and the government could appoint them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Usually these were the key areas, key sectors, and the assistant ministers were appointed for the most significant sectors. As a rule, not always, but this was up to the estimate and up to the decision of each single minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But it seems to me that the decision of the government on the appointment of the assistant ministers did not specify for which particular sector or area the assistant minister was to be tasked. This was up to the decision of the minister which was taken later on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really answer that. I can't really say anything about these decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I believe there's just another article that I find interesting here, it is Article 69 of this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In B/C/S this is on page 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Actually, this is a general article about all the units of the administration saying that the decision was to be made about individual appointments, so I believe that this is an article that's relevant for different acts that were adopted at MUP.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and if any other law -- unless any specific law relevant for the particular area stipulated otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. It seems to me that on page 21, line 19, it says -- it should be "assistant minister."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, as we don't have paragraph 69 in English and since it is a very short paragraph, perhaps the witness could be asked to read it slowly so that whatever he is commenting on could be on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. A good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you now see Article 69?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The decision shall be used to decide on individual administrative and other individual issues in line with the law and other regulations." What does this mean? In administrative procedure and in line with the law, the administrative procedure was to be carried out in line with the law on administrative procedure which is a different law from this one. Here it is simply a possibilities provided to use decision to decide on individual administrative matters and other individual matters but in line with the law, and this is the law on administrative procedure or other regulations. And the administrative procedure in the Republic of Serbia was regulated by the law on general administrative procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1049. P1049.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's go back to criminal liability in the MUP and the relevant decree. You told us yesterday that when a member of the MUP commits a crime, the administration and his chief are informed. Did it ever happen to you that you did not get approval to prosecute a member of the MUP who was guilty of a serious offence?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It only happened in the case of less serious offences.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I was only asking about the serious offence. On what basis did you ask for approval from the chief of sector?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a good question. Until 1992, chiefs of Secretariats could do this independently. In 1992, when the public security sector got Radovan Stojicic for the chief, employees of the Secretariats, chiefs of Secretariats, became treated as people on assignment, and they had no independence in decision-making. Prior to 1992, chiefs of Secretariats were appointed by the minister with the approval of the government, and they had certain latitude of independence. And in 1992, when Mr. Radovan Stojicic became chief of that sector, he made a decision called decision on assignments, and chiefs of Secretariats became assigned employees just like any other employees. And chiefs of Secretariats were no longer able to take any action. They could not even move a person from one job within the Secretariat to another job. They could not start any sort of proceedings before they asked chief of sector for approval. This approval was later given by heads of administrations. Chiefs of Secretariats at the time were not allowed to inform the media about any incidents, security incidents, in their territory before they got approval from the chief of sector. This was ordered by a dispatch that Mr. Stojicic sent to all Secretariats. And this is why we had to seek approval from sector chief or from heads of administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me get this right. He was deputy minister, Mr. Stojicic; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was deputy minister and sector chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But -- and in the absence of the minister, he stood in for the minister and had all the minister's powers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the minister's absence, he exercised all the minister's powers and responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And normally the deputy minister and the -- the deputy [as interpreted] minister does not have any other authority except the authority delegated to him by the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation is a bit different when he is at the same time sector chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In says in the transcript "deputy minister." It should be "assistant minister." Lines 23 and 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we do have to slow down a bit, both of us, because we waste more time on correcting the record than we save time by speaking fast. In practice, for serious violations of work obligations, did it ever happen to you that you did not get approval to continue proceedings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in relation to serious violations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during the war, a decree on Internal Affairs in the state of war was adopted, and you acted pursuant to that decree?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was adopted sometime in early April, if I remember correctly. I had to act under that decree for a very short time. I was chief of SUP until the 16th. After the 16th, all this legislation and everything that had to do with the work of the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica was no longer of great interest to me, and I believe the reason is understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: During the war with this decree, the rules on disciplinary accountability changed and the chiefs of SUPs were authorised to start and conduct first instance proceedings, disciplinary proceedings?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this decree was adopted on the 7th or the 8th of April, and by the time it got handed down to the SUPs, I did not have much time to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have D101.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I think we've mentioned this a moment ago. This is the instruction on the performance of Internal Affairs for reserve forces of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these instructions were signed -- this directive was signed by the minister himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But is it also true that in addition to this directive, the minister also issued orders to call up and engage reserve personnel biannually, I believe?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, reserve personnel could not be called up at all until the relevant order by the minister was issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D103.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, is this the order you just mentioned? This one is dated 25 December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have P52, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, could you explain to us the significance of this instruction in the practical work of law enforcement officials?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Every police station in the territory of the Republic of Serbia determined the necessary number of sectors. Sectors could be of the first category or other. Thus, the police station commander would suggest to divide the territory of the station into sectors. This proposal goes to the competent administration of the ministry. When the competent administration issues its approval, approves the proposal, then these sectors are identified on the territory of the police station. In order to carry out police work in a certain sector, a directive or instructions were needed. And this is precisely instructions on the organisation and implementation of law enforcement activities in the security sector. Various law enforcement activities in the security sector are identified, and it is also specified what should be in the file, in the dossier of the security sector. Every sector had its own dossier, and this dossier was prepared by the leader of the security sector. So every security sector had a leader appointed to it, and this leader was followed by a certain number of policemen. They constantly monitored the security situation in their sector and informed the police station commander. The police station commander would then identify further necessary activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While we are talking about this, could you tell us what is considered to be regular police work, regular security work, and what would be special or extraordinary security work?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, regular security work would be in peacetime, no major disorders, no major demonstrations or inter-ethnic clashes, no particularly grave crimes with elements of violence. In different conditions, if all these indicators are higher, then those would be extraordinary circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have D1004-1902.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, you will soon see on the screen the instruction on information and reporting. Unfortunately, we don't have a translation. We still haven't received it. Could you tell us how informing and reporting was regulated in the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was adopted in 1994 by the minister, and this governs internal sharing of information within the Ministry of Interior. And as far as internal -- sorry, external informing is concerned, it is specified what kind of information can be given by chiefs of SUP to outside parties, other agencies, and the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it about informing and reporting on security incidents to be submitted to certain identified beneficiaries?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it right that unlike the army the police reports incidents and phenomena, whereas the army reports on activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, you can put it that way, conditionally speaking, even among theoreticians there are various interpretations of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We won't go into that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Conditionally speaking, you could say that this was a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, informed by the practice, what did daily reporting mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every Secretariat of Internal Affairs in the territory of Serbia would register, record everything, current incidents and phenomena in the field of security for the past 24 hours. This would have to do with law and order, general crime, economic crimes, violent crime, organised crime, traffic safety, and other areas related to security. All the police departments and police stations would submit these reports to the duty service at the seat of the ministry. The chief of the duty service would record all this in the log-book of daily incidents. From this log-book of daily incidents, the most important incidents are extracted to be included in the summary of the most important incidents, and this daily report is submitted to the operation centre. If an incident is extremely important and needs to be reported immediately, that incident would not wait to be entered into this daily bulletin. Instead, a dispatch is sent immediately to the competent administration in the ministry. And later on when the time comes, it also becomes part of the daily bulletin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the daily bulletin shows everything important that happened in the territory of the SUP in the past 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only the most important things. Lots of things happen every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You worked in conformity with this instruction; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you submitted daily reports also to the MUP staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I got some linguistic suggestions. When you say "events" it is being interpreted into English as "incident" and my associates suggest that it should be "event."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness will say what he believes should be said. The official interpreters will interpret it as they think it appropriate. If you want to dispute a particular interpretation, you should raise it, and we will go through the process of reviewing the tape. But off the cuff suggestions for changing the words is not really going to be a practical way, Mr. Djurdjic, of dealing with this. I hope that will guide you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I did not know about that rule. Because when I speak to a witness in Serbian, I understand what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We have been talking about reporting to the MUP staff. Did you also submit these reports to them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you submit to them any other reports other than this daily bulletin that you submitted to the MUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chiefs of Secretariats had to report to the head of the MUP staff every morning, and to inform him of all current events and incidents that were not covered by the bulletin.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us perhaps mark this document for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've mentioned a number, Exhibit D1004, I think, when introducing this document. Is that a 65 ter number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D232, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I should have said marked for identification pending translation, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I believe it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we will have the first break and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could I please have the Exhibit 1036.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a decision whereby you were sent to the SUP Kosovska Mitrovica to perform the tasks and duties of chief of Kosovska Mitrovica Secretariat as of 1st of January, 1997. Am I right to say that this decision was made by Mr. Radovan Stojicic who was chief of the sector at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that he made this decision with his authority of an assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And chief of sector as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the following paragraph where it says: " While performing the aforementioned tasks ..." And then here we have the entitlements that you had, salary and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was pursuant to the law up to 50 per cent of the monthly pay and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And how were your per diems paid out, through which body?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the Secretariat in Mitrovica, and 50 per cent through the Secretariat in Kragujevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you talking about the salary?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Salary, and 50 per cent in Kragujevac and per diems in Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Once again I'll have to correct something in the transcript. This decision was made by the deputy minister, who at the time was chief of public security sector Mr. Radovan Stojicic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And everything else I previously asked, your answer would have been the same?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean deputy minister or assistant minister? I see it's translated here as "deputy minister," that's what you mean? Just keeping you consistent, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djurdjic, thank you. Well, this is exactly what I asked, Mr. Stojicic was deputy minister and chief of the sector at the time when this decision was made. Later on we will show a different decision. Could we please see the Exhibit P77.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, now we'll see this in the English as well, all right. This is the decision on the termination of your tasks and duties dated 15th of April, 1999. Was this decision made by the authority of the minister? Is it stated here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the very end of this decision, can you see that this decision was made by the assistant minister chief of sector?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you now tell us what is the difference between the assistant minister and the deputy minister in this particular function?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The deputy minister stood in for the minister at the time when he was absent and he had all the rights and obligations of minister. Whereas an assistant minister did not have these rights and obligations. He was only charged with one specific sector within the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see the Exhibit P78.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a decision dated April the 15th on Lieutenant-Colonel Vucina Janicijevic being appointed chief of Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica; am I right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this decision was made by Minister Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the time when all of this was happening, so when you receive the decision stating that you have completed your tasks and Mr. Vucinjevic [as interpreted] was appointed, do you remember that this decision on the fact that you were terminated at this position was made at the level of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the Exhibit P75.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is the decision on the assignment of Mr. Bosko Petric to perform duties and tasks of chief of Secretariat in Pristina, and it was made by the minister; am I right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the Exhibit P79.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, am I right to say that the decision of the 15th of April, 1999, on the termination of the tasks in Pristina was made by the assistant minister chief of public security sector at the time, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic, upon the authority or authorisation of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So on the basis of these documents, am I right to say that whenever such a decision was made by an assistant minister, it was made upon the authorisation of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, we mentioned Momcilo Stojanovic. Could you please repeat, as far as you know, what was his position with his staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late October, early November 1998, he came to the MUP staff in Pristina. In early 1999, given that in the previous year the Ministry of the Interior had a plan of housing, construction of housing facilities in Kosovo and Metohija in order to resolve the housing situation of the employees of the ministry. According to that plan, in the territory of SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica a building was supposed to be constructed with between 30 and 50 apartments. So he came to SUP in Kosovska Mitrovica to talk to the contractors in relation to the construction of this building. And on basis of this, I can assume that he was in charge of these housing issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear that he was sent there also in order to arrange the business premises that were used for human resources purposes and some other personnel functions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could conclude that since he carried out the tasks pertaining to housing, so these were investments, so possibly he was also in charge of maintenance of facilities in which different organs of the police in Kosovo and Metohija were situated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the Exhibit D99.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I believe you haven't seen this decision before.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the very first time I can see this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the second page of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you recognise this signature of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please take a look at item 3 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In order not to come back, under items 3 and 4 we can see what were the tasks that he was supposed to assist in?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what the decision states, but I answered previously what was it that he dealt with when he came to the Secretariat in Kosovska Mitrovica. I wasn't aware of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that under this item 1, General Momcilo Stojanovic was assigned as a member of the staff to fight terrorism in the territory of autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And here it says: "Pursuant to the decision to establish the ministry staff for the prevention of terrorism DT 01 ..." number and so on?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but while I was in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, I did not see this decision; I did not even know that this particular staff was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. But then these tasks under 1 also include the task that you mention, housing; and item 2 mention other tasks as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, because these are similar tasks. They all pertain to investment, regular maintenance, and investment into new facilities. This is all rather similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you worked in this organisation for years, in this particular decision nothing -- there's no mention of salary which is normally included in decisions of this type?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but these persons mentioned in this decision most probably had a decision on being sent somewhere which encompassed provisions on salary, so possibly it wasn't necessary to repeat the same provisions here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. This date, there, is 2nd of October, 1998; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please now see the Exhibit P1044.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, you saw this decision yesterday. It was shown to you. It's dated 5 October, 1998. It's signed by assistant minister chief of sector, Vlastimir Djordjevic. It's the decision to send General Momcilo Stojanovic to perform a security job in the autonomous province of Kosovo-Metohija on the the authority of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the salary stipulated in this decision and this decision was in fact made to be submitted to the financial services section so that these benefits can be received, the financial services section always receives such decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this decision, that kind of decisions, are always submitted also to the personnel services.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But in the previous decision we did not have this salary provision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't necessary because the decision to send someone already included provisions about salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. But the decision of the minister was dated 2nd of October, and this one is dated the 5th October?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's practically the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you agree that this decision dated the 5th is in fact a follow-up of the 2nd of October decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, basically.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D38.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, is it the decision to send Colonel Dusan Gavranic to perform to the job of chief of SUP Gnjilane, this was done on December 17, 1998, and the decision was made by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you know perhaps Dragan Bozovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see Exhibit P259.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you recognise the signature of Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and do you recognise this format?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that by this decision, the minister sends Colonel Dragan Bozovic to the MUP staff in Pristina to a security related position?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we see that from the heading. From the preamble.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that under Roman numeral III, it is envisaged that for his work, Colonel Bozovic shall be accountable to the head of the MUP staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is written in paragraph 3 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see P82, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, is it the case that this decision, adopted by the assistant minister public security sector chief, Vlastimir Djordjevic, is a decision to send Colonel Miroslav Mijatovic -- sorry, it's the decision to terminate Colonel Miroslav Mijatovic as department chief in the police administration?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did the Assistant Minister Djordjevic take this decision on the authority of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see P80.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a decision to terminate the assignment of Colonel Milenko Arsenijevic also taken by Vlastimir Djordjevic, assistant minister, on the 1st of April, 1999. Is it also taken on the authority of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not right because this is not on the termination. It is the decision to send.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P144.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. Cvetic, the previous decision, P80, to send Milenko Arsenijevic was taken by public [Realtime transcript read in error "state"] security sector chief assistant minister, Vlastimir Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. You said state security sector, and it's public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the authority of the Ministry of the Interior on the 1st of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now we see a decision to terminate captain Milan Cankovic on the position of special security related tasks taken on the 30th of May, 1999. It's again taken by the assistant minister sector chief, Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic, on the authority of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You did see Mr. Milan Cankovic at the staff during your tenure?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him, and we spoke on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was chief of communications?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: At the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Assistant Chief of Staff for radio communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's what you know?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I believe that's contained in the decision to establish the staff which we can see because that material is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, we'll come to that. But let me ask you: If General Djordjevic sent Mr. Cankovic there by virtue of the decision you spoke about from June 1999, that was his original authority; right? His inherent powers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was the decision to set up the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that was in accordance with the rules?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, why does the minister take the decision to terminate the person?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the chief of sector is able to take all decisions on the authority of the minister, including decisions to send and decisions to terminate; and the minister can do the same. That means, what I'm trying to say is this: The minister of the interior is at the head of the ministry, and he controls the work of the ministry in its entirety. And he is accountable and responsible for the overall state of affairs in the ministry. The minister of the interior is therefore the most responsible persons for all the affairs of the ministry. For certain areas of work, he can authorise other persons to decide in his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You are completely right, but now we are on the ground. If the chief of the public security sector was authorised to take the decision to set up the staff under the rules of internal organisation, was he really authorised? Did he have the power?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's the power he has under the rules?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Why would he then take the decision to terminate Milan Cankovic on the authority of the minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he, chief of sector, or the minister, in order to pull out a person from Kosovo and Metohija, they have to issue a decision. A decision can be withdrawn only if a decision existed to send somebody.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you understood my question. If the chief of sector had powers inherent in his office it to send someone, why did he need the authority of the minister to withdraw the person?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened in the case of this Cankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let us then see --

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these things, and I cannot claim anything with any certainty. I can only speak about specific situations. I don't know whether he had blanco authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: We are not talking about blanco authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's see D100.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, if we look at the preamble of this decision, what legal grounds are cited here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "Pursuant to Article 10 of The Rules on the Internal Organisation."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So based on that, the chief of sector is authorised to form staffs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Staffs, commissions, and other working bodies, but this does not include this staff, or may include that particular staff. It all depends on interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So did he form the staff under this decision, this decision to set up the staff in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And we see the missions of that staff formulated?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under (a) that is to suppress terrorism and armed insurgency?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then we see the following points, (b), (c), (d), et cetera?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In sub-item (a), the provision should be read in the context of the task from para 2 because it's the task of the staff to plan, organise, and guide. Each word carries a particular meaning. And to coordinate the work of Secretariats and stations of border police in the territory of Kosova-Metohija in performing for complex and important duties and assignments that involve column(a) the suppression of, [indiscernible], disorder, terrorism, and armed insurgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You are right; I'm not interpreting this. I'm just saying that these tasks are identified for the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, let us turn the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let's look at para 5. To whom, according to this paragraph, was the head of staff answerable?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For his own work and the work of the staff, the head of staff is answerable to the chief of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And he is answerable for the status of public security, public is very important?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he could not be answerable for any other situation, even if someone wanted him to be because he is heading the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now look at para 6.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "The staff leader shall inform" -- "shall report to the chief of the public security sector any significant security incidents, the measures undertaken, and the results of those measures." This should be actually expanded to say "significant events in the area of public security." That would be more precise. But since the chief of the public security sector is concerned, he can only be answerable for the situation in public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Para 3 envisages technical assistance to be lent to organisational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the relevant decision on appointments will be made in due course?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that decision was made on the 11th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see P760.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a decision on the appointment of members of the staff. I believe it was made on 11th of June, 1998. We will see that later on on the next page. But, Mr. Cvetic, was this decision also made pursuant to Article 10 of the rules?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the preamble of this decision, we can see that it was made pursuant to Article 10 of the rules on the internal organisation of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
