utterances.text: Thank you. Under item 1, would this decision Major-General Sreten Lukic was appointed staff leader; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under item 2 Lieutenant-Colonel Radoslav Dinovic, assistant chief of the SUP in Smederevo, was appointed deputy leader of the staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Was Radoslav Dinovic really deputy leader of the staff from this moment onwards?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radoslav Dinovic came as deputy leader of the staff in 1997 in June of 1997 when Colonel Mijatovic was withdrawn from the position of the leader of the staff and assistant chief of traffic police administration Colonel Aco Vasovic was appointed leader of the staff. At that time, Mr. Radoslav Dinovic was appointed deputy leader and we would normally call him deputy Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. That was before, but with this decision we can see the relevant time is 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was still chief -- deputy Chief of Staff, but he remained in that position for a very brief period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Goran Radosavljevic was appointed assistant leader of the staff for interventions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Major Zarko Brakovic was appointed assistant staff leader for police affairs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the second half of 1998 and while you were there, was he indeed an assistant leader of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in reality he carried out three different tasks; he had three areas of responsibility. He was at the staff an assistant leader of the staff for police affairs, in SUP Pristina he was head of the police department, and he was also commander of the -- of a PJP detachment and later commander of 124th Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm just asking about members of the staff. So could you see him at all the meetings of the staff when the staff members were present including the SUP chiefs or?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely did it happen for the staff meeting to take place with all the members that are listed in this decision. Normally it will just be some members of the staff that are relevant for the specific topic discussed that were present at the meeting. So Zarko Brakovic attending the meetings depending on the contents discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. But can you believe me that Mr. Brakovic told us that he never received this decision and that he was not a member of the staff starting with this date and until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, he was in the staff. And as I told you, he carried out three duties. He had three groups of responsibilities. So he was head of the police department, commander of a detachment, and member of the staff. So he can always tell you that at a given moment of time, he did not carry out one duty but another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But I believe the witnesses tell us the truth when they come before this court?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously everything that I'm saying here I'm saying on the basis of the information that I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Undoubtedly, Mr. Cvetic. Major Miodrag Rsumovic was supposed to be a coordinator for white-collar crime. Could you see him in the period from mid-1998 until the end of the period that you spent there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him until mid-1998, but when we started with anti-terrorist actions and onwards, I couldn't see him attending any of the staff meetings because white-collar crime was not a topic discussed by the staff, but we rather discussed the issues pertaining to anti-terrorist operations. So his attendance was not required. Before that period, I saw him in person and he personally would come to the SUP Kosovska Mitrovica to see the head of department for fighting white-collar crime at SUP Kosovska Mitrovica, and this is where I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Novica Zdravkovic was appointed coordinator of general crime. Did you see him?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you also see Major Radovan Vucurevic who by this decision appointed assistant leader of the staff for border police aliens?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about him, but I do not know him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, we'll come to that later. Milan Cankovic was appointed assistant leader of the staff for radio communication?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that already.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the counsel could kindly repeat the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in the second half of 1998 I can't claim with certainty that he was present at the meetings, but he was present at the meetings before that time. Because the issues discussed in the second half of June 1998 until the end September 1998 during the time of anti-terrorist actions, different persons attending the meetings because different issues were discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are leaping too far ahead. You will notice at about line 15 that your whole question was missed. You were asked to repeat the question. We've got the answer. We don't know the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, I see your microphone is switched on but the interpreter didn't hear what you said. I am afraid you'll have to start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I -- this is the second time that I have to repeat this question. I apologise. Okay, we have to repeat this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I'm reading from this decision, and then I'm asking whether the persons mentioned in this decision were seen by you in the period between the -- after the second half of 1998 at the staff. We all know what is written in the decision; this is not contested. I'm just asking whether you saw Milos Deretic in the second half of 1998 until the period when you left Kosovska Mitrovica at the end of April 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "at the staff"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking at the meetings held in the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometimes he was there, sometimes he wasn't. Depending on the issues that were discussed at the meetings, there are minutes which -- of these meetings which list all the attendees of these meetings. Usually there were chiefs of Secretariats but not always. Obviously commanders of PJPs, but not all always. The SAJ commanders, but again not always. And some other persons from the ministry or from the staff. The meetings were attended by those persons that were charged with the current issues, the issues that were discussed by the particular meeting so that were included in the agenda of that meeting. And the staff as such did not have a single rumour facility where all the members of the staff would be present. Rather, they carried out their regular duties, and when needed, they would be invited to come for a meeting. It was only the staff leader and his deputy who actually sat there, who had their positions there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cvetic, could you believe me that Milos Deretic, when he was a witness here, he told us that he never received this decision and that he was not a member of the staff pursuant to this decision in the period between mid-1998 and the end of 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm saying that pursuant to this decision, he was; but I'm not saying that he was presents at the meetings of the staff after this particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Then maybe it was a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But he was sometimes at the meetings of the staff possibly before this period. I know that I saw him there, but possibly not in line with this particular decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is exactly what I'm trying to clarify. The next person is Miroslav Krajcic an assistant in charge of quarter master?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and he was also -- he also had the duty at the SUP in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Gojko Celebic who was assistant leader of the staff for logistics?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about him, but I do not know him in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Dobrasin Krdzic who was in charge of medical issues?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I know about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And also we have another person, Rasko Milenkovic, who was in charge of surveillance analysis or assistant leader of the staff for surveillance analysis?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about him, but I can't remember his face.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 2 of this decision states that the members of the expanded staff were going to be the heads of Secretariats of -- in the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, this is what is stipulated under item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have to provide an explanation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These heads of Secretariats were members of the expanded staff, but they did not have any individual duties in the staff, because members of the staff normally have to have specific duties so their respective areas of responsibility and it needs to be clarified who they answer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I can agree with you, but here it is simply mentioned that you were members of the expanded staff.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, if the Chamber can allow me to make a parallel: It is similar to the former constitution of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia which stated that any citizen who, with a weapon or otherwise, could contribute to the defence from the aggressor was considered to be a member of the armed force, well this stipulation in reality meant nothing at all because it wasn't specific enough. So this is something very similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly see the Exhibit P57.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is a decision that you didn't see prior to yesterday, although the Prosecution knew about it, even the last time you witnessed here, and the Defence team also knew about this the last time you witnessed here.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked any questions concerning this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, this is why I'm going to do it right now. You said that undoubtedly this was a decision made by Mr. Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I see the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but there are so many different decision, so could I just see the signature. Yes, Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic, and I can recognise this signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Let us then start from the end of this document in order to save some time. In item 6 is it true that the minister decided that the decisions to establish a staff of 21st of April, 15th of May, and 11th of June ceased to be in effect?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but this makes no sense because this is not in correspondence to the actual situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 1 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this decision was made on the June the 16th, 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that within this decision, Sreten Lukic was also appointed leader of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but leader of the staff for suppression of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm pointing this out because he was leader of the MUP staff in Pristina. And while he was in Pristina, all the time he was leader of the MUP staff. And while I was SUP chief, I was invited to the meetings of the MUP staff in Pristina, and not to the meetings of the staff for the suppression of terrorism. So the logical question can be raised, how come that chief of Secretariats and commanders could attend meetings of the MUP staff in Pristina if that staff was already abolished?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you think that it was abolished? Well let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you showed that to me. You showed me the decision whereby that staff was abolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, we will not draw any conclusions. It is up to the Chamber to draw the conclusions. But according to this decision, was David Gajic appointed deputy leader of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And was Radoslav Dinovic appointed assistant leader of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And he was in charge of interventions and operational planning?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And under the previous decision, Radoslav Dinovic was an assistant leader of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Milorad Lukovic was an assistant head of special operations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that he was employed by state security section?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now we have as the chief of JSO [as interpreted], Mr. Trajkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Special anti-terrorist units --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry SAJ, not JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- there was a decision taken in June 1999. We did not have this position until then?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had an appointment for interventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is an appointment for special anti-terrorist units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, we have Major Goran Radosavljevic as assistant head of Special Police units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the previous staff for interventions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers stop overlapping, please. They are speaking at the same time the witness is answering before the question has finished. We cannot follow in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, we Mr. Lukovic he is in both decisions concerning mechanised units, but he is now assistant?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the second page, but I know that he was -- I know the person, and I know he was in charge of the work you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but as a coordinator? Assistant chief of staff for mechanised units in the first decision as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then we have Novica Zdravkovic; he is now in charge of criminal investigations and operations?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And he was coordinator for general crime earlier?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now we have Radovan Vucurevic, border affairs and foreign nationals. He was also on the previous decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him. I heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then we have Milorad Rajicic; he was in both appointments, the first and the second one. And he is assistant. And then we have Milan Cankovic, chief of communications, he was also on the previous decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And then we have Dobrasin Krdzic as chief of medical corps in both decisions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you see that Milos Deretic, Gojko Celebic, Zarko Brakovic, and Miodrag Rsumovic are missing from this decision?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this could be interpreted in another way. What you ask me, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But let me put another question: Does this decision include people from both public security and state security?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's only one person from state security. And now I see the expanded staff also includes head of centres from state security.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This decision involving members of both sectors, this decision could only be taken by the minister of the interior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that in para 2 of this decision, please look at it, the minister stipulated that the task of the staff is to plan, organise, guide, and employ organisational units of the ministry, and also the seconded and attached units to suppress terrorism in the province of Kosovo-Metohija?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written in this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And in the next paragraph of para 2, the staff plans, organises, and guides the work of organisational units in performing more complex security tasks?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Secretariats are meant here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, in para 3, what did the minister envisage?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the head of staff should be answerable to the minister for the state of affairs in their purview, and to report to the minister on all the activities, measures taken, and the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the minister did not make this available to you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic -- I said para 3, right? Can you tell me, to whom was this decision delivered? What does it say?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision says that the decision was sent to the head, the deputy, and members of the staff as well as the minister's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your work, regardless of this decision, nothing changed, did it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But the relations between the staff and the head and the superior have changed with this decision on intersectorial activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P67.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, just repeat your last answer.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered "yes" because that follows from the material that has been shown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now we are on P67. Mr. Cvetic, have you got the gist of page 1?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but at that time I wasn't --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I know you were not. Let's go on. This is dated 31st of May, 1999. It's the decision to establish the ministry staff for the suppression of terrorism. And in para 1 we see the full title, The Staff for the Suppression of Terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija based in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And again Sreten Lukic, now lieutenant-general is appointed head of staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe he got this decision as of 13th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And we see Mr. Milenko Arsenijevic here, even during your tenure, he was member of the staff for awhile, Colonel Milenko Arsenijevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we move to page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Blagoje Pesic was on the earlier staff as well; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Pesic was in charge of reserve police squads at the staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, by virtue of this decision dated 31st of May, Sreten Lukic is again appointed head of staff for the suppression of terrorism in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, we see on page 2, in this decision the minister appoints Miroslav Deretic chief of communications; correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that members of the expanded staff under this decision and the previous decision include heads of centres of RDB, the state security sector?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This decision is also a decision on an intersectorial staff; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So do I.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The task of the staff under Roman numeral II is the same as in the decision of the 16th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The accountability and responsibility of heads of staff is formulated in the same way, their responsibilities for the work of the staff that is?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move to the last page, page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: By virtue of this decision dated 31st of May, 1999, did the minister render null and void the decision to establish the staff for the suppression of terrorism, DT 01 number so and so of the 16th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This decision was sent to the head of staff, the deputy, the assistants, members of the staff, and the minister's office?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's also written.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvetic. Just one more point.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 1 in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, was this decision taken by the minister of the interior pursuant to Article 7 of the Law on the Interior?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if I am allowed to give the witness a hard copy to look up the legal basis for the decision. Can we have P57.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I saw that it was marked and highlighted and that is why I was indicating no, but if it is to look up the legal basis, I have no objection to him being shown it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, if it's for that one purpose, the witness may see your document. But otherwise, it is heavily marked, and he shouldn't have it during your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He just needs to look up if it's indeed Article 7 in the preamble.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is Article 7, and on the basis of that Article 7, the minister was entitled to take this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, in view of your previous position, I want to go together with you through various dispatches, some sent by the minister, some sent through the public security sector down to your SUP Kosovska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see for that purpose, D004-1572, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you remember this dispatch from Minister Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, what was the political and security situation at the time when you received this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation was difficult and very complex. Terrorist attacks had escalated in the entire territory of Kosovo. A large number of policemen had been killed or seriously or lightly injured. There were attacks on the army, Serbs, Albanians loyal to the state of Serbia. There had been numerous attacks on the installations of the army and the Ministry of Interior. Roads were unsafe or completely unpassable for traffic. One could not move safely across the territory of Kosovo, especially not at night. All movement on the territory of Kosovo was practically restricted. So the situation was indeed very complex. The territory of Kosovo was no longer under the control of the authorities of Serbia, that is the Ministry of the Interior. Parts of the territory had been captured by the terrorists, and the terrorists controlled various population centres. By that time, they had already started taking hold of individual businesses and enterprises.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I see that in this dispatch, you are informed that the Kosovo Diplomatic Mission would start to work soon in keeping with the Milosevic-Yeltsin Agreement?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think that's the time when the Pristina-Pec road was cut off. Was it at that time or later?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was later in July. But the road what was unsafe even at this time. Traffic was made very very difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What was the situation with roads in the territory of the SUP of Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very hard. It was the hardest in the territory of Srbica which belongs to the area of Drenica, so that the road from Srbica via Rakos, Rudnik, and Padaliste to Pec, or rather, Istok and Pec, was frequently blocked and unsafe. On that a road, a large number of terrorist attacks were launched against the police, against public transportation, and there were kidnappings of passengers. For a while, that road was completely blocked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is its date?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 17th of June, 1998. But my infallible assistant, Ms. Marie O'Leary, wants to remind me of something. That we tender only pages 2 and 3 because page 1 is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D233, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing, please. Could I have page 2 because this is a dispatch, and attached is a joint statement by President Milosevic and Mr. Yeltsin, and the statement of the prime minister, which is referred to in the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are looking at me, Mr. Djurdjic. What are you wanting me to do?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm waiting for to you receive this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's been received as Exhibit D233.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have time for another document. 65 ter 04079.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this dispatch, Mr. Cvetic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you a moment ago, the first dispatch we discussed, it was sent by the minister to the MUP staff and to the SUPs in Pristina, Gnjilane, Urosevac, Kosovska Mitrovica, Djakovica, Pec, to chiefs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to SUP chiefs in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And this document we're looking at now, it was sent to all the SUPs in Serbia and all these other addressees?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the state security and the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 3 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is signed Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this Dispatch 2 mentions the diplomatic mission that is about to start working?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and the international humanitarian organisations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D234, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it may be time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will have the second break, and we resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, it seems that by time we are getting more and more tired, but we are nonetheless talking more and more quickly, so please let us try to slow down so that everybody can follow our conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the document 200 -- sorry, D001-2922.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, can you recognise the format of this document, and is this the signature of Mr. Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this was sent to the staff, MUP staff in Pristina, but after this date, you received this agreement on the OSCE Verification Mission; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D235, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly see the Exhibit D208.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is the decision on the formation of the MUP collegium of 4th of December, 1998. In order not to waste time, we will see the signature later on, and you will be able to confirm whether you can recognise the signature or not. Here we can see that the decision was made to set up a collegium, and we have a list of persons that were going to be the members of this collegium.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, under item 1 we can see Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic, assistant minister and chief of public security department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Item 2, Colonel-General Radomir Markovic, assistant minister and chief of state security department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And under three, Major-General Nikola Curcic who was assistant minister and deputy chef of RDB and director of the security institute, so all three functions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And under 4, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic, assistant minister?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So at this moment on 4th of December, we can see that some persons held different functions and some others held only one, i.e., they were assistant ministers?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what this decision stipulates.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we kindly see page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here we can see additional two members: chief of the crime police, Dragan Ilic, and chief of SUP of the Internal Affairs in Belgrade, Mr. Duric; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under item 3, we can see who was to attend these collegium, Mr. Krstic as chief of the analysis administration, who was supposed to take minutes, and also Captain Pantovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Danilo Pantovic; that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And upon an invitation by the minister, other persons could attend, whoever he wanted to invite?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you recognise the signature of Mr. Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it on my screen. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document has already been admitted into evidence, so we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you know the exhibit number, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. D208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask for the document D002-0343.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may, Your Honours, to supplement what I was saying. Even earlier there was a collegium of the minister of the interior; so in this decision, I cannot see that the previous decision was terminated so that the effect of the previous decision on the collegium of the minister was terminated for this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cvetic, can you see this dispatch, and can you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Later on, when we turn the leaf you will be able to see the signature, so it was dispatch sent by the minister to the MUP staff in Pristina and all the SUPs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the signature of Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, am I right to say that with this dispatch, the minister informed members of MUP in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija that if attacked, they could undertake measures to defend themselves, if attacked by terrorists?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the minister didn't need to inform them about this because the Law on the Interior stipulated the authorities of authorised officials; and if an authorised official was to be attacked, then the authorised official was supposed to react to this attack, so this was the task of any authorised official as stipulated by law. However, when we are talking about terrorist activities, individual police officers were not allowed to undertake any measures regardless of the legislative provisions, without an approval of the MUP staff or the ministry to undertake certain anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D236, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have D004-1579.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you briefly comment on this. This is a dispatch that was sent to all the chiefs of SUPs in the territory of Serbia and also to the staff in Pristina and border police stations.

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was simply a relayed decision of the government of the Republic of Serbia as to what was supposed to happen after the declaration of the state of the imminent threat of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the date is 24th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is when the aggression started.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we possibly enlarge this. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch dated 25th of March, 1999, sent by the minister to all SUPs and to the staff and to the organisational units of the public security sector in the seat. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this copy is rather illegible, so I can't really comment on it unless I can see it in a hard copy version, so I would kindly ask to see it in a hard copy version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I underlined certain parts of the text, so I'm not sure that it will be appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could you please advise me on that. I didn't write anything, but I did highlight certain parts of the text.

utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Pass it over, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I take it there is not yet a translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, the translation is pending. We gave very many documents to be translated. A majority of those have been translated already, but there is a small number that is still pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can remember this dispatch. It followed the proclamation of the state of war, and it concerned the measures that had to be undertaken following the proclamation of the state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please mark this document for identification in order to be included into evidence once we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D238 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. [Microphone not activated] Could I please have the document D004-1592.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember -- actually, you can't remember, you haven't seen it yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a dispatch of the MUP staff sent to all the SUPs and do you remember -- and also detachment commanders. Do you remember this dispatch dated 15th of July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what was the situation like at the time when you received this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the security situation? Well, the situation was similar to the one I described previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At this time, was there already danger that certain, sort of, imminent danger -- that certain populated areas could be taken over by the forces of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that certain companies were already taken over and obviously they attempted to put certain inhabited areas under their control as well. But I would like to say the following: This is a dispatch of the staff of the ministry. So the staff of the ministry existed on July the 15th because previously we can see a document proving that there was a decision from June of that year which abolished this staff. So as chief of SUP, I received dispatches from the MUP staff in Pristina and at this time, the MUP staff in Pristina was in operation. It wasn't abolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Under item 3, what is the instruction of the staff?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During the operations, fire exclusively at targets outside populated places or where it is known reliably that there are no civilians."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So the instruction of the staff was to take care about the civilians?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes. This was a general position, to take care about the civilians, but on the ground, there were also some problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have this document tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D239, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, these anti-terrorist activities, were they prescribed by this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were the preparations for the anti-terrorist activities. The anti-terrorist activities initiated on July the 25th, so this was the face of preparations.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But under item 1 it says, In the period from the 14th to the 20th of July, plan, organise, and carry out active combat operations from a distance against terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: All right. So item 1 stipulates as follows: In the period from the 14th to the 20th of July, plan, organise, and carry out combat operations against terrorist forces?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what item 1 stipulates, but anti-terrorist activities commenced on 25th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Those were planned activities, but from the 14th until the 27th, these activities are to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. But who, with what resources and objectives, that's not written. This is just the general formulation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D109, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Look at paragraph 3, please. How did it work in practice?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it worked like this: Since personnel from Secretariats of Internal Affairs was deployed in Kosovo and Metohija within PJP units and other special units, in the event that a police officer was killed, we, chiefs of SUPs were obliged to report to the Secretariats from whose territory this personnel came.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that the anti-terrorist operations were not planned, organised, and carried out from the 16th of June until the 1st of May, 1999, while you were there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was exclusively in the jurisdiction of the MUP staff. The Secretariats didn't do this job, but, of course, they provided certain information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D108, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I'd like to know about this dispatch that you now see on the screen, and that the staff sent to all the SUPs and chiefs of SUPs and unit commanders in Kosovska Mitrovica. Did you have this information?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as chief of SUP, I did not have this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In criminal investigations, did you act pursuant to the orders given here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We applied this to all the persons who needed to be investigated and interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 04124.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is again a dispatch from the staff addressed to all SUPs in Kosovo. Is this a format you recognise?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you have any knowledge or did you take any action pursuant to paragraph 1 concerning the issuing of documents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that members of the Siptar ethnic community, as stated in this dispatch, did not carry personal identification documents. I'm not aware that these documents were destroyed. That I do not know, but I do know they did not carry IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Regarding this filling in and destruction of bunkers and trenches in the territory of Kosovska Mitrovica, do you know that the work was done? Did the SUP take any steps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a dispatch dated 9 August, 1998. And in the territory covered by SUP Kosovska Mitrovica, I'm not aware of any locations that were cleared from terrorists and later backfilled by construction machines. We did engage construction machinery to build protective shelters and other things that PJP units needed.

utterances.text: As Exhibit D240, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D001-2923.

utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, do you recognise this format?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The staff addresses the minister requesting that means of communication be supplied?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do we have the correct document? It's a newspaper order.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it's not a newspaper order. It's a letter from the staff to the ministry asking that these newspapers be supplied to ensure adequate daily information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sure it will be central to our decision, Mr. Djurdjic. It will be received.

utterances.text: As Exhibit D241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have D004-1599. Can we have page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, this is another dispatch from the staff dated 16 September, 1998, to detachment -- to the chiefs of SUP and detachment commanders. Did you receive this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this issue raised here was often emphasised at staff meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D242, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D004-1603, please. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I see here that this went to Djakovica. Is this again a format you recognise?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this dispatch perhaps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Anything particular you want to add?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing particular, but we acted in accordance with this dispatch and put up check-points.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D243, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D004-1607, please. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from the staff sent to chiefs of SUPs in KiM, 29 September, 1998, do you remember it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cvetic, I'd like you to cast your mind back to this period and illegal possession of weapons. You told us yesterday that according to the law on weapons and ammunition there was a ban in place on the possession of long arms by civilians and there were no licenses issued for that type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This calls for voluntary surrender of such weapons from missing in Amnesty. How was this carried out in Kosovska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBINKO CVETIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, even earlier it was emphasised at staff meetings that in certain villages, especially after 1996 and 1997 after the well known events in Albanian, large quantities of weapons from armouries in Albania had been smuggled into the territory of Kosovo. And many villages, especially in the Decane district, Drenica district, and Shala district had that sort of weapons. At that time, a corridor was established across the Junik mountains, Djakovica, Decane, Glodjane, and Jablanica, Drenica, Cicavica, leading to Bajgora; that is, along the Kosovo border from south to the north. At staff meetings, and this dispatch orders the same, it was ordered that Secretariats should look into the situation in their own areas and see how many such weapons had been smuggled in from Albania. Those were Chinese-made weapons, usually automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, hand-held launchers, and RPGs. In order to Amnesty the citizens and free them of criminal liability, it was agreed at that time to call on the citizens to surrender such weapons voluntarily at the level of villages and at the area of Mahalas. They could simply leave their weapons at a designated site without leaving their names or any personal information on the condition that the weapon had not been involved in any crime. In Kosovska Mitrovica, we did not do a lot of work. In fact, we did not perform too well in this area; but some other Secretariats did, especially those in the border area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, D004-1825, please. We'll get page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think you've already answered my question on this document. It's dated 2nd October, a dispatch from the staff to SUP chiefs in Kosovo. They inform you of the Amnesty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to have this document admitted with your leave.

utterances.text: Is there a translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't know. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D245 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I think we have come to the time for adjournment for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You are well over halfway, are you, Mr. Djurdjic? We will adjourn now. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m.
